claims.text: A thin, coherent B2-structured NiAl interlayer at HEA multilayer interfaces will shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
Conventional deposition of HEA multilayer coatings yields incoherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
Diffusion-mediated creep tends to dominate in HEA multilayers with incoherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
An ultrathin NiAl interlayer below 100 nm can be deposited between HEA layers.
The introduced NiAl interlayer will foster coherent interfaces.
Diffusion and dislocation creep mechanisms are both active at approximately 600–900 °C under the proposed constant-load conditions.
The NiAl interlayer provides an ordered B2 crystal structure.
The NiAl interlayer enhances interface coherency.
The NiAl interlayer reduces lattice mismatch at the HEA multilayer interfaces.
Reduced lattice mismatch decreases fast diffusion pathways associated with the interfaces.
A coherent, ordered NiAl layer acts as a barrier that reduces effective interfacial diffusion paths.
Suppression of interfacial diffusion limits atomistic diffusion responsible for low-stress creep.
The NiAl diffusion barrier promotes dislocation nucleation and glide in adjacent HEA layers.
The NiAl-modified multilayer will have a higher creep activation energy than the baseline multilayer.
The NiAl-modified multilayer will show a stress dependence characteristic of dislocation-mediated creep.
The NiAl-modified multilayer will exhibit less creep strain at constant load than films without the NiAl interlayer.
HEA multilayers without NiAl interlayers primarily exhibit diffusion-mediated creep under the proposed test conditions.
The proposed mechanism transition is expected only in a mid-to-high-temperature and stress regime where diffusion and dislocation mechanisms compete.
At very low temperatures or very high stresses, one creep mechanism may dominate regardless of interface structure, making the transition indiscernible.
The creep response and long-term thermal stability of the NiAl interlayer depend critically on interlayer quality and thickness.
